name: Tsetse Fly Swarm
body:
TSETSE FLY SWARM
CR 6

XP 2,400
N Fine vermin (swarm)
Init +2; Senses darkvision 120 ft., scent; Perception +9

DEFENSE

AC 20, touch 20, flat-footed 18 (+2 Dex, +8 size)
hp 71 (13d8+13)
Fort +9, Ref +6, Will +5
Defensive Abilities swarm traits; Immune weapon damage
Weaknesses swarm traits

OFFENSE

Speed 5 ft., fly 30 ft. (average)
Melee swarm (1 Con damage and sleeping sickness)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 0 ft.
Special Attacks cling, Con damage, distraction (DC 17), disease

STATISTICS

Str 1, Dex 15, Con 12, Int —, Wis 13, Cha 2
Base Atk +9; CMB —; CMD —
Skills Fly +10, Perception +9; Racial Modifiers +8 Perception

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Cling (Ex)

If a creature leaves a tsetse fly swarm’s square, the swarm takes 1d6 points of damage as dozens of insects tenaciously cling to the victim. A creature with tsetse flies clinging to it takes 1 point of Constitution damage at the end of its turn for the next 1d4 rounds. As a full-round action, the creature can remove the flies with a DC 18 Reflex save or by immersing itself in water. High winds or any amount of damage from an area-affecting effect destroys all clinging flies. The save DC is Dexterity-based. Once a group of clinging flies has dealt 4 points of Constitution damage, the flies detach and disperse to digest their meal.

Disease (Ex)

Tsetse flies are bearers of a terrifying and deadly disease common to the jungle, known to most locals as sleeping sickness.

Sleeping Sickness: Swarm—injury; save Fort DC 17; onset 1d2 days; frequency 1 day; effect 1d4 Wisdom damage and target is fatigued, cure 2 consecutive saves.

Taking a dose of arsenic grants a +4 alchemical bonus on the saving throw. Horses take a -4 penalty on their sav-ing throw against sleeping sickness but zebras are immune.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm forests and swamps
Organization solitary, pair, pestilence (3–6 swarms), or plague (7–12 swarms)
Treasure none

Thousands of species of insects on the savannah and torrid forests, but few inspire more dread than tsetse flies. They carry a debilitating disease known for sapping the vitality of its victims, bringing on a dreadful lethargy and slow death to humanoids and their livestock and pets. Only high winds, drought, and torrential rain consistently keep them at bay, but thankfully their tendency to gather in buzzing swarms waxes and wanes with fluctuations in local prey populations, and this combined with their short lifespan and competition for food keeps their numbers under control.

Endemic throughout the sodden lands of the tropics, the parasitic affliction known as “sleeping sickness” is spread when flying insects inject tiny parasites into their unsuspecting victim’s bloodstream, thus inducing fever, headache, joint pain, swelling of glands in the back and neck, and most notably fatigue. The disease gradually infects the brain, causing confusion, reduced coordination, difficulty keeping track of time, and insomnia.

While exceedingly dangerous, even when administered by a practiced healer, the best cure for this disease is dosing the patient with the poison known as arsenic.
